Unique pair-index and orientation coordinates separate the forest partition from binary support. Conjugates of the single flip give exactly D_I; intersecting both coordinates proves all IP. This uses the permutation realization, not merely an abstract wreath-product isomorphism.

The four Q formulas are proved by actual conjugation of the new transposition. Mixed intersections remove a shared s or t. In the 11/11 case terminal intervals are nested; after a shared swap and cancellation on the smaller root support, the remaining diagonal permutation preserves both partitions. The rooted-branch counterexample confirms that nesting cannot be dropped.

The two end groups are the already proved paired wreath marking and the independent unequal paths. Their intersection consists exactly of row-preserving paired permutations, the diagonal middle group. The explicitly retained classical end criterion gives IP. Transitivity and a pure transposition give the full symmetric group; further leaves use the first common theorem.

The adjacent product cube isolates the disjoint involution; conjugation of the bridge and cancellation prove the direct product without source primitive-group classification. Rank two has product order four. Rank three uses the explicit four-point block system for the D8/D12 intersection. Higher rank uses exactly the retained endpoint central extension and end criterion, with the middle group identified by point stabilizers and the adjacent cube.

In each larger subgroup a local full symmetric image and an actual pure transposition give the actual t, hence the outside involution tau. In the common-label subgroup the outside exponent equals the core sign, excluding tau. The same supported core and outside transitive action, joined by the bridge, prove the full S_(2r-1) for every source parameter. This is the source already established disproof, not a new conjecture answer.
